independent_replay.method: Downloaded original CI ZIP; verified SHA256; extracted prebuilt pinned baseline and modified Wasmtime CLI compilers; recompiled exact same WAT to fresh AOTs with x86_64-unknown-linux target; required byte-identical AOT and disassembly against CI archive; independently enumerated decoded native bytes and division instructions; independently evaluated finite arithmetic with Python divmod and wrap/rotate semantics, compared 8 values and 7 distinct-site traps per compiler; replayed original source-pinned audit (positive and eight mutation controls) and compared its JSON byte-for-byte.

assurance_limits: This audit reuses exact precompiled experimental compilers; it independently reruns their emitted-code and guest-execution results but does not independently rebuild compilers from source.
AOT hash equality, native bytes, and finite guest traps are not a formal proof of Cranelift pass, SSA, dominance, liveness, trap metadata table, target-state, flag or poison correctness.
Unsigned i64 arithmetic only; signed overflow not part of the selected admissible semantics; no global compiler or cross-target claim.
No ZenoFCIS-new instruction discovery, runtime throughput improvement, or whole-AOT reduction is established.
The archive digest is a source/artifact integrity reference, not a guarantee of correctness.
followup: Review actual compiler-pass IR verification and trap-table mapping; test full backend and nonmatching cases before upstream proposal. Keep experimental branch draft.
